text.en: Which folders of a SQL project should normally be excluded from Git?
bin/ and obj/ (build output, including the .dacpac)
The folder containing table .sql files
The post-deployment scripts folder
The .sqlproj file

explanation.en: Build outputs are reproducible and belong in CI artifacts. Source .sql files, deployment scripts and the project file must be committed.

example.en: .gitignore: bin/ obj/

text.en: A GitHub Actions workflow must deploy to Azure SQL without storing any Azure client secret in GitHub. What should you use?
OpenID Connect federated credentials with azure/login (client-id, tenant-id, subscription-id) and permissions: id-token: write
A service principal secret in a repository secret
The SQL admin password in the workflow YAML
A personal access token in the code

explanation.en: OIDC lets GitHub obtain short-lived Azure tokens through a federated trust — no stored secret. Repository secrets (b) still store a secret; c and d are leaks.

example.en: Configure a federated credential on an Entra app/managed identity for repo:org/repo:environment:production.

text.en: A developer accidentally committed a connection string with a password and pushed. They removed it in the next commit. What must happen?
Rotate (change) the password immediately — it remains in Git history
Nothing; the later commit deleted it
Make the repository private
Rename the file

explanation.en: Git history (and forks/clones) still contains the secret. Treat it as compromised: rotate it, then optionally rewrite history. Visibility changes don't revoke copies.

example.en: Enable push protection to block such commits in future.

text.en: Two branches merge without textual conflicts, but the merged project no longer builds because a view references a column renamed in the other branch. What does this illustrate?
A semantic conflict — always rebuild and run CI after merging
A Git bug
That SQL projects can't be merged
A permission error

explanation.en: Git merges text, not meaning. The project build's reference validation catches these semantic conflicts — one reason to require CI status checks before merging.

example.en: Branch protection: require the 'build-sqlproj' check to pass on the merge result.

text.en: For each item, answer Yes if it should be committed to the repository.
The .refactorlog file
Publish profiles without credentials
A production connection string with password
Post-deployment reference data scripts

explanation.en: The refactorlog preserves rename intent; profiles and deployment scripts are source. Credentials never belong in Git.

example.en: Pipelines inject credentials or use identity-based auth.

text.en: Which GitHub feature makes a secret available only to jobs that deploy to 'production', after that environment's protection rules pass?
Environment secrets
Repository variables
README badges
Issue templates

explanation.en: Environment-scoped secrets are released only to jobs referencing that environment, after required reviewers/wait timers approve. Variables aren't for secrets.

example.en: jobs.deploy.environment: production

text.en: Order a GitHub flow for a schema change.
Create a short-lived feature branch from main
Edit .sql files and commit
Open a PR; CI builds, tests and generates a deploy script
Review, approve and merge to main; deployment pipeline runs

explanation.en: Branch, change, validate in PR, merge and deploy — the standard trunk-based flow.

example.en: Keep branches short to limit drift and conflicts.

text.en: Why include the generated deployment script (SqlPackage Script output) in PR checks?
Reviewers see the actual ALTER statements (e.g. table rebuilds or drops) that the declarative change will produce
It replaces the .sql files
It encrypts the PR
GitHub requires it

explanation.en: A small diff in a CREATE TABLE file might generate an expensive table rebuild. Showing the computed script makes impact visible during review.

example.en: Upload deploy.sql as a workflow artifact or post a summary comment.

text.en: Which two GitHub features help prevent secrets from being committed? (Select 2)
Secret scanning
Push protection
GitHub Pages
Discussions

explanation.en: Secret scanning detects known secret patterns; push protection blocks pushes containing them. Pages and Discussions are unrelated.

example.en: Push protection rejects a push containing an Azure storage key.

text.en: Which statement about SQL database in Microsoft Fabric source control is correct?
It integrates with Git (GitHub or Azure DevOps) and represents the database as an SDK-style SQL project
It only exports .bak files
It requires SSDT on Windows
It doesn't support source control

explanation.en: Fabric's Git integration syncs workspace items, with SQL databases stored as SQL projects that standard tooling can build and deploy.

example.en: Commit from the workspace Source control pane.

text.en: Two developers modified the same stored procedure on different branches and Git reports a conflict. What's the right resolution process?
Merge both intended changes in the .sql file, rebuild the project and run tests before completing the merge
Pick one version at random
Delete the procedure
Resolve it directly in production

explanation.en: Resolve like code: combine the logic, validate with build and tests. Random picks lose work; production edits create drift.

example.en: Use VS Code's merge editor, then dotnet build.

text.en: Complete the workflow so azure/login can use OIDC.
id-token
packages
issues
client-secret
tenant-id
runs-on

explanation.en: OIDC requires the id-token: write permission so the job can request a token; no client secret is stored. tenant-id is still required, and runs-on is a job setting.

example.en: The federated credential's subject must match the repo/branch/environment.

text.en: A team keeps a 'database' branch alive for months while app development continues on main. What problem is most likely?
Branch drift and large, risky merges with many conflicts
Faster releases
Automatic synchronization
Smaller dacpacs

explanation.en: Long-lived branches diverge; integrating late surfaces conflicts and semantic breaks. Prefer short-lived branches and feature flags/expand-contract patterns.

example.en: Merge to main at least daily.

text.en: Match each secret need to the best storage approach.
GitHub workflow authenticating to Azure
API key needed only by production deploy jobs
App runtime reading a third-party API key
App connecting to Azure SQL
OIDC federated credential (no secret)
GitHub environment secret
Azure Key Vault via managed identity
Managed identity with Entra auth (no secret)

explanation.en: Prefer secretless identity wherever supported; otherwise scope secrets narrowly (environment) or keep them in Key Vault.

example.en: The fewer stored secrets, the fewer rotations and leaks.

text.en: What is the main reason to keep one object per .sql file in a SQL project?
Clean, focused diffs and fewer merge conflicts
SQL Server requires it
It encrypts objects
It speeds up queries

explanation.en: Per-object files make reviews and history clear and reduce overlap between developers. It's a convention, not an engine requirement, and doesn't affect runtime.

example.en: Tables/Sales.Orders.sql, Procedures/Sales.GetOrders.sql

text.en: For each statement about GitHub secrets, answer Yes or No.
Secrets are masked in workflow logs.
Workflows from forked-repository pull requests receive repository secrets by default.
Secrets can be defined at organization, repository or environment level.

explanation.en: GitHub masks secret values in logs, withholds secrets from fork PR workflows (pull_request event) by default, and supports three scopes.

example.en: Use environment secrets for production credentials.

text.en: When should app code and the SQL project live in the same repository?
When they're released together, so one PR can change schema and code atomically
Never
Only for Fabric
Only when the database has fewer than 10 tables

explanation.en: A shared repo keeps coordinated changes in one review. Separate repos fit shared databases with independent consumers, using versioned dacpac packages.

example.en: Monorepo: /src/Api and /src/Database/Sales.sqlproj.

text.en: Branch A renames column Orders.Amt to Total (with refactorlog). Branch B adds a procedure using Orders.Amt. Both merge cleanly in sequence. What will catch the problem first?
The project build after the second merge (unresolved reference to Amt)
Git's merge algorithm
Nothing until production
Query Store

explanation.en: Reference validation fails because Amt no longer exists in the model. That's why CI must build the integrated result (e.g. require up-to-date branches before merging).

example.en: Branch protection: 'Require branches to be up to date before merging'.

text.en: Which workflow trigger runs CI validation for changes proposed to main?
on: pull_request (branches: [main])
on: schedule only
on: release
on: issues

explanation.en: pull_request events validate proposed changes before merge. Schedules run periodically, release triggers on releases, issues on issue activity.

example.en: on: { pull_request: { branches: [main], paths: ['src/Database/**'] } }

text.en: How can a workflow run only when database files change?
Use a paths filter on the trigger (e.g. paths: ['src/Database/**'])
Rename the repository
Use a cron schedule
It's not possible

explanation.en: Path filters limit triggers to relevant changes, saving CI minutes and noise.

example.en: on: { push: { branches: [main], paths: ['src/Database/**'] } }

text.en: Which two practices reduce merge conflicts in a SQL project team? (Select 2)
Use SDK-style projects (globbing, no per-file project entries)
Integrate small changes frequently via short-lived branches
Put the whole schema in one giant .sql file
Edit production directly

explanation.en: Globbing and frequent integration minimize overlapping edits. One giant file maximizes conflicts; production edits create drift.

example.en: Trunk-based development suits database projects well.

text.en: Complete the trigger so CI runs for PRs into main affecting the database folder.
pull_request
deployment
fork
paths
files
folders

explanation.en: pull_request with branches and paths filters scopes CI precisely. 'files'/'folders' aren't valid keys.

example.en: Use paths-ignore for docs-only changes.

text.en: Where should non-secret configuration values (e.g. Azure tenant ID, client ID for OIDC) be stored in GitHub?
GitHub Actions variables (vars context)
Hard-coded in every workflow
In a public gist
In commit messages

explanation.en: Variables hold non-sensitive configuration and can be scoped like secrets. IDs for OIDC aren't secrets but centralizing them avoids duplication.

example.en: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}

text.en: Answer Yes or No about merge conflict handling for SQL projects.
Conflicts are usually localized to individual object files.
A clean textual merge guarantees a valid schema.
CI should build the merged result before completing a PR.

explanation.en: Per-object files localize conflicts, but semantic breakages slip through clean merges, so building the merged result is essential.

example.en: GitHub merge queues build the combined result before merging.

text.en: Which approach keeps secrets out of a publish profile that needs a target connection?
Pass the connection (or use Entra/OIDC auth) from the pipeline at deploy time instead of storing it in the profile
Base64-encode the password in the profile
Store it in a comment
Put it in the README

explanation.en: Encoding isn't encryption, and comments/READMEs are plain text. Inject at runtime or avoid secrets entirely with identity-based auth.

example.en: sqlpackage /Action:Publish /Profile:prod.publish.xml /TargetConnectionString:"$CONN"

text.en: Order the steps to respond to a leaked database password found in a public commit.
Rotate the password (or disable the login) immediately
Review audit logs for misuse during the exposure window
Move the app to secretless auth (managed identity) or a secret store
Enable push protection to prevent recurrence

explanation.en: Contain first, investigate, remediate the root cause, then prevent. History rewriting can follow but doesn't replace rotation.

example.en: Treat any exposed secret as compromised.

text.en: Why do teams prefer expand/contract (backward-compatible) schema changes in a branch-per-feature workflow?
Schema and app can deploy independently without breaking the running version
It removes the need for code review
It makes dacpacs smaller
It disables triggers

explanation.en: Additive changes first, removals later, let old and new app versions coexist — essential for zero-downtime deployments.

example.en: Add NewColumn → app writes both → backfill → app reads new → drop old.

text.en: In GitHub, how are changes typically proposed and reviewed before merging into main?
Pull requests
Issues
Wikis
Releases

explanation.en: Pull requests carry diffs, reviews and status checks. Issues track work; wikis document; releases package versions.

example.en: PR = review + CI gate before merge.

text.en: A database is shared by several applications owned by different teams. How might the schema be versioned for consumers?
Separate repo for the SQL project, publishing versioned dacpacs (e.g. NuGet packages) that consumers reference
Each app keeps its own copy of the schema
No versioning
Email scripts to teams

explanation.en: A dedicated project with versioned packages gives a single source of truth and explicit upgrades for consumers. Copies drift; emails aren't version control.

example.en: SDK-style projects support package references to dacpacs.

text.en: Which two settings reduce the risk of a malicious pull request from a fork stealing deployment credentials? (Select 2)
Keep production credentials in environment secrets with required reviewers
Avoid running untrusted fork code with pull_request_target plus checkout of the PR head
Expose secrets to all workflows on all events
Store credentials in workflow YAML for transparency

explanation.en: Environment protection gates secret release behind approval; pull_request_target runs with repository secrets in the base context, so checking out and executing fork code there is dangerous. Broad exposure and YAML credentials are leaks.

example.en: Use pull_request (no secrets) for fork validation builds.

text.en: Match each Git concept to its description.
Branch
Commit
Merge conflict
Pull request
Movable pointer to a line of commits
Snapshot of changes with a message
Overlapping edits Git can't reconcile automatically
Proposal to merge with review and checks

explanation.en: Basic Git vocabulary underlying the branching and PR bullets of the study guide.

example.en: feature/add-discount → PR → main.

text.en: A DBA hot-fixes an index directly in production. What's the right follow-up in a source-controlled workflow?
Add the change to the SQL project via a PR so the source of truth matches production (otherwise the next deployment may drop it)
Nothing
Delete the repository
Disable future deployments

explanation.en: Out-of-band changes cause drift; if DropObjectsNotInSource is on, the next publish removes the hotfix. Back-port it to source.

example.en: Drift detection before deployments catches these.

text.en: Is each of these a secret that must not be committed? Answer Yes or No.
An Azure OpenAI API key
The name of the database
A SQL login password

explanation.en: Keys and passwords are secrets; a database name is configuration (though you may still parameterize it per environment).

example.en: Secrets → secret stores; config → variables/profiles.

text.en: Which option lets a workflow read secrets from Azure Key Vault without a stored credential?
Log in with OIDC (azure/login) and read secrets with an identity that has Key Vault access
Store the vault's master key in GitHub
Make the vault public
Email the secrets

explanation.en: Federated identity grants the workflow an Azure token; RBAC on the vault controls access. No secrets live in GitHub.

example.en: az keyvault secret show --vault-name kv --name ApiKey

text.en: Which GitHub feature batches PRs and validates each against the latest main plus earlier queued PRs before merging?
Merge queue
Draft PRs
Labels
Projects

explanation.en: Merge queues build the combined result to catch semantic conflicts between concurrent PRs — very useful for SQL projects.

example.en: Requires status checks to run on merge_group events.

text.en: Why should a CI workflow for a SQL project request only the minimum GITHUB_TOKEN permissions (e.g. contents: read)?
Least privilege limits damage if a step or dependency is compromised
Builds run faster
dotnet build requires it
It enables OIDC automatically

explanation.en: Scoped token permissions are a supply-chain safeguard. They don't change speed; OIDC needs id-token: write explicitly.

example.en: permissions: { contents: read }

text.en: Complete the .gitignore for a SQL project.
bin
Tables
Scripts
obj
Procedures
Security

explanation.en: bin and obj hold build output; object folders are source and must be committed.

example.en: The CI pipeline uploads the dacpac from bin/Release as an artifact.

text.en: A federated credential is configured with subject 'repo:contoso/app:environment:production'. A workflow job without 'environment: production' tries azure/login via OIDC. What happens?
Login fails — the token's subject claim doesn't match the federated credential
Login succeeds with full access
GitHub prompts for a password
Azure creates a new credential automatically

explanation.en: OIDC trust is bound to the subject (repo + environment/branch). Jobs outside the trusted context can't obtain tokens — a powerful way to restrict deployments to approved environments.

example.en: Add separate federated credentials per environment with distinct Azure roles.

text.en: Which statement about versioning reference data (lookup rows) with the schema is true?
Reference data scripts in source control give reviewable history and consistent environments
Reference data should only live in production
Git can't store SQL data scripts
Lookup data never changes

explanation.en: The study guide explicitly asks to manage reference/static data in source control — typically idempotent post-deployment scripts reviewed via PR.

example.en: PR diff: + ('PKR', N'Pakistani Rupee')

text.en: Which two are valid ways for a GitHub workflow to authenticate a deployment to Azure SQL with Entra ID? (Select 2)
OIDC azure/login, then use the workload identity's token for the connection
Service principal with a client secret stored as a GitHub secret (less preferred)
The sa password in the YAML
Anonymous SQL access

explanation.en: Both use Entra identities; OIDC is preferred because no secret is stored. sa passwords and anonymous access are unacceptable.

example.en: Grant the deployment identity a database role sufficient for schema changes (e.g. db_ddladmin + needed permissions).

text.en: Answer Yes or No about Git history and database code.
git blame can show who last changed a line of a stored procedure.
Reverting a schema commit automatically reverts production.
History helps auditors trace when a column was added.

explanation.en: Git provides authorship and timeline; production changes only via a deployment of the reverted state (which may involve data loss checks).

example.en: git log -p -- Tables/dbo.Orders.sql

text.en: Which branching strategy is generally recommended for teams practicing continuous delivery of database changes?
Trunk-based development / GitHub flow with short-lived branches
One branch per developer kept for a year
No branches, everyone commits to production
A branch per table

explanation.en: Short-lived branches merged frequently into main keep integration continuous and conflicts small.

example.en: Feature flags let incomplete features merge safely.

text.en: A PR changes a column from NVARCHAR(100) to NVARCHAR(50). What should reviewers check in the generated deployment script?
Whether existing data exceeds 50 characters — the change may lose data and be blocked or fail
Nothing; shrinking is always safe
Only formatting
The PR title

explanation.en: Narrowing types risks truncation; BlockOnPossibleDataLoss stops it by default. Reviewers should verify data and plan migrations.

example.en: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dbo.T WHERE LEN(Col) > 50;

text.en: Order the setup steps for OIDC-based deployment from GitHub to Azure.
Create an Entra app registration or user-assigned managed identity
Add a federated credential matching the repo/environment subject
Grant the identity the needed Azure and database permissions
Use azure/login with id-token: write in the workflow

explanation.en: Identity, trust, authorization, then usage. Skipping authorization yields 403s even when login works.

example.en: Separate identities per environment limit blast radius.

text.en: What is a 'status check' in a GitHub pull request?
An automated result (e.g. CI build/test) reported on the PR's commit
A manual comment
A Git tag
A database index

explanation.en: Status checks come from CI and can be required by branch protection before merging.

example.en: Required check: 'build-database'.

text.en: Which practice best supports traceability between a production schema version and its source?
Tag/version builds and record the commit SHA in the deployment (e.g. dacpac version or a deployment log table)
Deploy from developers' laptops
Avoid commit messages
Delete old commits

explanation.en: Linking deployments to commits enables audits, rollbacks and drift analysis. Laptop deployments lose traceability.

example.en: Post-deployment: INSERT INTO dbo.DeploymentLog (CommitSha, DeployedAt) VALUES ('$(CommitSha)', SYSUTCDATETIME());

text.en: A repo secret DB_PASSWORD exists. Answer Yes or No.
Writing it with echo in a step shows it masked as *** in logs.
Masking makes it safe to send to any third-party action.
Pinning third-party actions to a full commit SHA reduces supply-chain risk.

explanation.en: Masking only hides values in logs; any action receiving the secret can exfiltrate it. Pinning actions to SHAs prevents tag hijacking.

example.en: uses: azure/sql-action@<full-commit-sha>

text.en: Which file format does SQL database in Fabric write to Git for each database object?
.sql files in an SDK-style SQL project
Binary .mdf files
Power BI .pbix files
CSV data exports

explanation.en: Objects are stored as declarative .sql files inside a SQL project, enabling standard diff/review and tooling.

example.en: dbo/Tables/Orders.sql in the repo.

text.en: A dev wants each PR to deploy to an isolated database for integration tests. Which approach fits?
Spin up an ephemeral database (e.g. SQL Server container or temporary Azure SQL DB), publish the dacpac, run tests, tear down
Deploy every PR to production
Share one dev database for all PRs
Skip testing

explanation.en: Ephemeral databases isolate PRs and give reliable tests. A shared dev database causes interference; production deployments of PRs are unsafe.

example.en: services: mssql: image: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest

text.en: Match each risk to its control.
Concurrent PRs break each other after merge
Secrets accidentally pushed
Unreviewed deployments to production
Stored Azure credentials in GitHub
Merge queue / required up-to-date checks
Push protection & secret scanning
Environment with required reviewers
OIDC federated credentials

explanation.en: Each GitHub capability mitigates a distinct source-control or deployment risk.

example.en: Together they form a secure database delivery pipeline.
